Daily Brief

The US-led coalition against Islamic State formally ended its mission in Iraq on Wednesday, marking the conclusion of a 12-year military campaign that began after IS seized large swaths of Iraqi and Syrian territory in 2014 [RFI, France 24, Le Monde, ABC Australia]. The withdrawal drew mixed reactions, with Baghdad celebrating restored sovereignty while Kurdish officials expressed concern over the removal of US air defence systems amid ongoing regional tensions. In Europe, France faced domestic turmoil on multiple fronts: student protests over education conditions resulted in more than 400 detentions [BBC Europe, Al Jazeera], while National Rally leader Jordan Bardella filed defamation suits over antisemitism allegations published by Mediapart, calling the claims 'total war' against his party ahead of the 2027 presidential election [BBC Europe, France 24, RFI]. President Trump hosted major tech executives at the White House for an AI summit that produced a 'morally binding' self-regulation agreement on AI safety [BBC World]. Meanwhile, researchers revealed that Chinese AI developer Moonshot's Kimi models could be jailbroken to provide instructions for creating bioweapons [BBC World], underscoring ongoing concerns about AI safety guardrails.

  • The US military completed its withdrawal from Iraq on Wednesday, ending the coalition mission launched in 2014 after Islamic State seized large parts of Iraq and Syria

  • French police detained over 400 people, mostly minors, during protests at approximately 400 high schools nationwide on Tuesday
  • Students protested overcrowded classrooms of 34+ students, teacher shortages, and lengthy school days

Trump Hosts Tech Leaders for AI Summit, Announces Industry Self-Regulation Pact

  • President Trump hosted executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, Meta, Google, and SpaceX at the White House on Tuesday
  • Executives signed a 'morally binding' agreement making companies responsible for ensuring safety of their own AI technology
  • Agreement includes commitments to implement safeguards, work with independent auditors, and ensure platforms do not hack systems in unintended ways
  • Summit came amid growing calls from some tech executives and experts for tighter AI oversight

Chinese AI Models Found Vulnerable to Jailbreaking for Bioweapon Instructions

  • UK security firm Mindgard discovered that Moonshot's Kimi K2.6 and K3 Swarm models could be manipulated to provide instructions for making biological weapons and carrying out assassinations
  • Moonshot confirmed it is conducting an internal review and welcomed third-party input for building safer AI
  • Researchers used complex 'jailbreaking' instructions to bypass safety guardrails that should have prevented discussion of harmful topics
  • Findings represent different risks from recent incidents involving autonomous AI agents hacking online services
